title: Proper direct image, base change and projection formula for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and $p\colon X\to Y$ proper between standing schemes.

1. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ bounded below,
   $Rp_*(K[1/\ell])\simeq(Rp_*K)[1/\ell]$; for $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ bounded below and
   $F/E$ finite, $Rp_*(K_F)\simeq(Rp_*K)_F$ and $Rp_*(K_{\Qlb})\simeq(Rp_*K)_{\Qlb}$, via the
   canonical maps.
2. $Rp_*$ maps $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$.
3. The proper base change and projection formula maps are isomorphisms on $\Dbc(-,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: For integral localization unfold rationalizationPushHom and apply localizedDirectImageComparison_isIso. Properness supplies qcqs. For a finite coefficient extension use isIso_derivedPushHom_padicSubfieldRingObjMap. For extension to the algebraic closure unpack the bounded-below witness N, install IsGE N and use isIso_derivedPushHom_padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl_app_of_isGE. These are the actual canonical derived push mates.

proof.text: For an integral bounded constructible pair, transport the coefficients by the proved continuous-function integer-ring isomorphism to the spectral integer-ring presentation, preserving bounded constructibility. The adic constructibility comparison identifies that predicate with constant-model bounded constructibility. Apply the projection clause of integralProperDirectImageAndFormulas. The coefficient/projection square and equivalence of scalar extension reflect invertibility back to the embedded integer coefficients.

source.place: paragraph (3), rationalization of integral formulas; existing integral models replace generator induction

proof.text: The scalar/projection square transports invertibility whenever the integral projection and the two push comparison components are invertible. The bounded constructible integral-to-E scalar functor is a localization, hence essentially surjective. Choose an integral model of each input, apply tensor and pullback preservation to its tensor input, use clause (1) for both push comparisons, and cancel the invertible scalar tensor and push factors. Naturality of the actual projection transformation transports the conclusion across the two input isomorphisms.

source.place: paragraph (3), rationalization of integral formulas; existing integral models replace generator induction

proof.text: For algebraic-closure inputs, descend each bounded constructible object to a finite subextension. Take a finite compositum and extend both models to it. Scalar transitivity identifies their algebraic-closure extensions with the given inputs. The finite-field projection formula just proved and the two bounded coefficient push comparisons give invertibility by the same scalar/projection square; tensor closure supplies the second lower bound. Naturality transports across the two input isomorphisms.

source.place: paragraph (3), rationalization of integral formulas; existing integral models replace generator induction

proof.text: Split the bundled rational coefficient equality into its two cases. In each case the conditional restriction has exactly the same functor, adjunction and unit-square-counit map as the existing finiteness-coefficient restriction: the preservation witnesses are proofs of the same proposition. Apply the existing proper base-change natural-transformation theorem and evaluate at the bounded constructible object.

The re-split is faithful. Of the 11 old steps: old 2 and 4 become the filtered-legs criterion; old 3 is the existing imported lem-sfb-subfield-push-iso; old 6 is covered by the existing push-counit node, the ringed monoidal-comparisons node and det-prop-scalar-six-pullback; old 7 and 10 become the exchange-normalization node plus existing projection-shift nodes; old 8 becomes the common-field node; old 9 becomes the projection-square node; old 5 and 11 stay as assembly steps 3 and 6. The four new nodes are statement-only and of comparable size, none restates a clause of the item, and the proof is 6 steps and 2585 chars. All four statements are true. (A) Bounded continuity via det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image, with the leg identity checked on the one-object and ell-tower cases. (B) Compositum F, then generators clause (3) with E:=F, then scalar-pullback clauses (2) and (3). (C) Both composites have matching types; this is the old step-9 transpose calculation. (D) Triangle identity, adjoint shifts, and agreement with det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-bc. Steps 1-6 and the hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates are verified; I found no cycle and no duplicate (I opened lem-sfb-qlbar-push-iso-proper, lem-sp-direct-image-change-ring-transpose and the continuity nodes), and no SGA. One fault, fixed: step 5 inverts the direct O_F-to-Qlbar push comparisons by part (1) without citing the coefficient cocycle. I added lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle to its uses and text; proof_deps is unchanged. Batch 5: lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison is general module-object/ringed-topos infrastructure (Stacks 07A4/07A6/0B56). It is not given by Poincare duality and cannot be replaced by that leaf, and three PASSed sfb nodes already cite it, so I accept it. The trf reach through def-sfb-dc-lower-star, the upper-lower adjunction, integral-models-generators and the base-change-morphism nodes is generic and already in the base item's closure; the closure diff adds no trf node. Accepted. Advisory: the existing lem-sfb-qlbar-push-iso-proper would give E-to-Qlbar directly, but the blueprint continuity route is legitimate.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
